t: Signing up and creating the account
s: How to create your login, and then the account that brings your venues together.
h: Your login The account The trial
b: Signing up takes two steps. First you create your own login, then the account that holds your venues, your team and the daily report. You won't need a bank card. On the sign-in page, click the No account yet? Sign up. link. Type your email address in the Email field. Choose a password of at least 8 characters in the Password field, then type it again in Password again. Press the Sign up button. Under the button, it says that by signing up you accept the terms of service and acknowledge the privacy notice. You can open both from there. On the Create your account page, type the name of your venue or company in the Account name field. You can rename it later. Check the Time zone field. We fill it in from your browser, but you can change it. In the Language field, choose the language for your daily report. Press the Create account button. The First steps guide then opens on its own. It walks you through adding a venue and setting up the daily report. Tip: If a colleague has invited you to an existing account, don't create a new one. Sign up from the invitation link and you'll land in the right account straight away. A new account starts with a 14-day trial. The article about the trial explains what's included and where to see how many days you have left.

s: Find your restaurant on Google, add it, and a few minutes later you'll see its latest reviews.
h: How to add it What you see next What we download first If you get stuck If you want to pause a venue
b: The account owner adds venues. You add the first one in the First steps guide and any others on the Venues page, using the same card. Open the Venues page in the Account group of the menu. In a new account, the First steps guide opens by itself instead. On the Add venue card, type the venue's name, with the city if you like, for example “Példa Bisztró Budapest”. Press the Search button. In the results, check the address and the number of reviews, so you're sure you're picking your own venue. Press the Add button. The First download card shows how far the download has got. First it shows the review count and average that Google displays, then how many reviews we've downloaded. It usually takes a minute or two, and you can carry on with the next step of the guide in the meantime. Until your first daily report is ready, the Today tab works from the downloaded reviews. It shows how many reviews we downloaded, their average, and how many negative reviews from the last 30 days are waiting for a reply. In the meantime, we write replies to the recent reviews that don't have one yet, except 4- and 5-star reviews with no text. You'll find those replies on the Replies tab. The venue's latest reviews, not its whole history. We don't write replies to the older reviews. You can see them on the Reviews tab. The daily report doesn't count the older reviews from the first download as new. Your first daily report comes at the hour you set. If that hour's already passed today, it comes tomorrow. If there are no results, add the city, or type the name exactly as it appears on Google. If a result says “Already on the list”, you've already added that venue. If your current plan has no room for another venue, the page will tell you. Then write to us. If the download fails, we'll try again in the morning. You don't need to do anything. Tip: Linking your Google Business Profile is a separate step. You don't need it to download reviews, but you do need it to post replies. Adding us as a manager on Google shows you how. On the Venues page, turn off the Active switch on the venue's card, and confirm with Switch off. While it's off, we don't download its reviews and it drops out of the daily report. Nothing's lost, and you can switch it back on at any time.

t: Adding us as a manager on Google
s: Add us as a manager on your Google Business Profile. Once we've accepted the invitation, we'll post the replies you approve.
h: The address you add On Google Checking Until it is linked Taking the access back
b: You'll get your reviews without it. Manager access does two things. It lets us post your approved replies on Google, and it lets the Listing page see your Business Profile. The account owner goes through these steps. Open the Venues page and press the Check connection button. If any venue isn't linked yet, the Linking to Google Business Profile card appears. It shows the email address to add as a manager. Copy the address. Open your Google Business Profile with the Google account you use to manage it as its owner. In the profile's settings, find the users and add a new one with the address you copied. Pick manager as the role and send the invitation. Google emails us the invitation. For now we accept these by hand, so the link won't work straight away. It starts working once we've accepted. Go back to the Venues page and press Check connection again. Look at the venue's card. If it says Linked, you're done. If it still says Not linked, press Check connection again later. If it still hasn't changed, let us know with the Feedback button in the menu. Nothing stops in the meantime. We still write the reply and you approve it. Then you copy it with one button and paste it in on Google yourself. Here's how: Posting a reply by hand, without Google access. You can remove our manager access on your Google Business Profile whenever you like.

s: Pick the time your daily report arrives, and connect Telegram if you'd like it there too.
h: The time Connecting Telegram Without Telegram The other two destinations
b: Every day at the time you set, the daily report sums up the reviews posted since the previous report, venue by venue. You can always read it in the app, and if you connect Telegram, we'll send it there too. The account owner can change these settings. Open the Settings page. At the top you'll see what time the report goes out, and in which time zone. On the Account card, pick the time in the Daily report time field. You can choose any quarter of an hour. Press the Save button under the Set-up guide card. A new account gets its report at 08:00 in the morning, in the account's time zone. On the Telegram destinations card of the Settings page, press Connect in the Daily report row. If the report's for you, press the Open it on Telegram link and start the chat in Telegram. If it's for your team's group, add the Telegram account named on the panel to that group. Then send the command shown on the panel in the group. The Copy button copies it for you. When the code comes through, the panel shows which chat it came from. If that's the right one, press Yes, there. The code works for 10 minutes. If it's run out, press Connect again. If you don't connect anything, the report is still made at the time you set. You'll find it on the Sent messages page, in the Account group of the menu, marked “Here only. No Telegram chat is connected.” Want your phone to let you know when it arrives? See Putting it on your phone. Reports by email are coming later. You can already set the switches on the By email too card of the Settings page. The Marketing destination gets the weekly rank summary, and Alerts gets the alerts. You connect both the same way. There's more in Alerts. Tip: Got a question? Ask it on the Assistant page, in the More group of the menu. It answers from your own reviews. More in The assistant.

s: BistroTech opens like an app from your home screen and can send you notifications.
h: On Android On iPhone Notifications on your phone
b: There's nothing to download from an app store. You add BistroTech to your home screen from your phone's browser, and from then on it opens without the browser bar. Open BistroTech in Chrome and sign in. If the Add to your home screen bar appears at the top of the page, press the Install button. Confirm when the browser asks. If you hid the bar earlier, you can install it from Chrome's menu instead. Open BistroTech in Safari and sign in. Open the Share menu. Choose Add to Home Screen, and confirm. Open the My login page by clicking your own email address in the menu. On the Notifications on this device card, press the Turn on button, and allow it when the browser asks. Tick what you'd like to hear about: A low review arrived, The morning report is in. We haven't tried notifications on every phone yet. If you've turned them on and nothing comes through, let us know with the Feedback button in the menu. On iPhone, notifications only work from the BistroTech you added to your home screen. They go to the device you turned them on for, so you'll need to turn them on separately on each one. We'll tell you about a low review when the instant alert is on in Settings and a Telegram chat is connected. The details are in Alerts.

t: What the numbers in the daily report mean
s: What counts as a new review, what you see for each venue, and what the parts at the end of the report are for.
h: What counts as new For each venue At the end of the report The analysis The same numbers on the Today tab
b: The daily report comes in two messages. The first has the numbers. The second is the analysis, and it only comes on days with reviews that have text. A review is new if the guest posted it since the previous morning report. Two reports never count the same review. If a report is made again, it gives the same number. If a guest rewrites their review, we don't count it again. The change shows in a separate part, as Changed and removed reviews explains. How many new reviews came in, and their average. The star breakdown, from 5 down to 1. The venue's Google rating and its total number of reviews. A red mark if a one-star or two-star review came in. Venues with no new reviews get one line each at the end of the list. Under them, the “Total” line has the numbers for the whole account. “Unanswered negatives”: reviews of 3 stars or fewer, no more than 14 days old, that have been waiting at least a day and don't have a reply we can see yet. The oldest comes first, and each one links to the review. “No fresh data”: venues where the download failed or was skipped. The next successful download catches up on them. If none of your venues got a new review, the report shows a warning. That's common for a smaller venue and doesn't mean anything's wrong. If you've connected Tripadvisor, a separate line shows the new reviews there. They're kept out of the Google numbers. The second message is built from the day's reviews with text. “Mentions by name” lists the staff members guests named. “Themes” shows what came up more than once. If there were no reviews with text that day, you won't get this message. The Today tab opens on the morning report's numbers and counts the same reviews. To see another period, use the Other period button. You can pick Report, Today (what's come in since the morning report), 7 days or 30 days (the last 7 or 30 morning reports). The stars for each venue are in the Full breakdown by star table, inside the Full breakdown part. On a phone, open both first.

t: The extra report lines and the monthly summary
s: 4 switches in Settings, for 3 extra lines in the daily report and a monthly summary.
h: Where to switch them The four switches The report's name In the weekly summary
b: On top of what's always in it, the daily report can carry 3 more lines. You'll only see them when there's something to say. In a new account, all 4 switches are on. Open the Settings page and find the Report card. Switch on or off what you want. Press the Save button under the Set-up guide card. The account owner sets the switches. Negatives waiting for a reply, per venue: under each venue's line, you'll see how many 1-, 2- and 3-star reviews are still waiting for a reply, and how long the oldest one has waited. We only count the ones that came in after we started watching the venue. Time of day line: if at least 3 negative reviews came in that day, and most of them fall in the same part of the day, the report tells you which. It's lunch, afternoon, evening or night. What counts is when the guest wrote the review, not when they visited your venue. Google removal line: if the review count Google shows has dropped by 2 or more since the last reading, the report says by how much. We don't flag a drop of 1, because that's just Google's own churn. Monthly summary to the group: on the first of each month, a short piece about the month before. We send it to the same Telegram chat as the daily report. If you haven't connected Telegram, you won't get a monthly summary either. On the same card, you can give the report a name in The report's name field. It goes at the top of the daily report and the weekly summary, in capitals. If you leave it empty, it says BistroTech. The weekly summary's “This week” list is partly built from the same 3 signals. So if you switch a line off, it drops out of the weekly list too (see The weekly summary).

s: Every Monday you get the week that's just ended, venue by venue, compared with the week before.
h: Which week What is in it The weekly rank summary
b: On Mondays, the weekly summary comes shortly after the daily report. It goes wherever the daily report goes: to Telegram, or to the Sent messages page if no chat is connected. The summary covers the last 7 days, up to and including yesterday, and compares every number with the 7 days before that. For each venue, the number of new reviews, and which way that's moved since the week before. For each venue, how many 5-, 2- and 1-star reviews came in, and the weekly average. The totals for the whole account. The names mentioned most, venue by venue. The themes that kept coming up during the week. The breakdown of your guests' review languages, when we know the language of enough reviews. The “This week” list, with up to 3 things to do. If there's no data for part of the week, the heading tells you how many days of data went into the summary. If you're watching search phrases on the Rank page, there's a second summary on Mondays, about your positions on Google Maps. It goes to the Marketing destination on Telegram, but only if you've connected it. Your rank on Google Maps and your competitors has the details. You can read both summaries again on the Sent messages page, under the Weekly summary kind.

s: When we send alerts outside the daily report, and where they go.
h: Instant alert on a low review Pattern alarm Error message
b: Besides the daily report, we send three kinds of alert to Telegram. All three go to the Alerts destination, so it's worth connecting that one too, on the Telegram destinations card of the Settings page. It works the same way as for the daily report. Open the Settings page and find the Instant alert on a low review card. In the Alert when the review is at most field, choose the number of stars. If you don't want the alert, choose Off. Use the two Quiet hours fields to set when we should keep quiet. Press the card's Save button. A new account starts at 2 stars. Once a review like that reaches us, we'll let you know within 15 minutes. Anything that comes in during quiet hours, we send together when they're over. If the Alerts destination isn't connected, this alert goes to the daily report's chat instead. If that isn't connected either, we've no way to tell you. During the day, we watch for two patterns at each venue. One is several one-star reviews coming in over a short time. The other is several guests lowering an earlier rating within a few days. We only look at Google reviews for this. We'll tell you about the same pattern once a day, and once more that day if the count reaches twice the threshold. This alert only goes to the Alerts destination. It can also name who needs to be told. You set that person on the Settings page, in the Who to notify on an alert field. If a venue has had several one-star reviews in the past 24 hours, a warning card shows up on the Today tab too. If the pattern looks suspicious, open a case for it, as Disputing reviews with Google explains. If something goes wrong on our side, like a venue's download, the Alerts destination gets a short message. Usually you don't need to do anything, because the next scheduled run catches up. Tip: Your phone can tell you about a low review too. Putting it on your phone shows you how.

s: How to find every review of one venue, one star rating or one word.
h: Search Quick filters More filters A review's card Notes and who handles it
b: The Reviews tab shows every review we've downloaded, newest first. At the top there's a search field and a few quick filters. On a phone, the Filters button opens the quick filters. Type a word in the search field, for example “goulash” or “waiter”, and we'll look for it in the text of your reviews. All: takes every filter off. Needs a reply: reviews of 3 stars or fewer that we don't see a reply to yet. 1 and 2 stars: the worst reviews. 5 stars: the best ones. All venues: pick one venue here, if the account has several. All sites: choose between Google and Tripadvisor here, if you've connected Tripadvisor. Under More filters you can also filter by stars, reply, sentiment and text, and set the order (Newest first or Lowest rating first). The number of matches is shown above the list. Tip: Your filters are kept in the browser's address bar too. Copy the address and send it to a colleague, and they'll open the same list. The stars, the guest's name, the time and the language. The analysis, meaning the sentiment, up to 2 themes and the staff named. A New mark if it came in since your last visit. Whether it has a reply yet, and a link that opens the review on Google or on Tripadvisor. The Notes, owner link under the review opens the team's own part. In the Assigned to field, you choose which colleague handles it. Under Internal notes, you write what you know about the case, and save it with the Add button. Only your team sees the notes, never the guest. Colleagues with the viewer role can only read them.

s: What happens when a guest rewrites a review, or when Google takes one down?
h: If the guest rewrites it If Google takes a review down
b: A review can still change after it's posted. The guest can rewrite it, or Google can take it down. We keep an eye out for both. On Google, a guest can leave one review per venue. When they rewrite it, Google sometimes gives it a new ID. To us it's still the same review, and we don't count it twice. The Reviews tab always shows you the latest version. We keep the old version too, so you can see what changed. The “Changed reviews” part of the daily report shows what changed from what, like 5 stars down to 1, or just the text. Reviews that went down come first, with their new text. The change isn't counted again in the report's numbers. If several guests lower their rating at one venue within a few days, we'll send you a pattern alarm. More in Alerts. Tip: You can also ask the Assistant page which reviews changed in a given period. Google sometimes removes reviews, for example when one breaks its rules. We can tell because the review count on your Business Profile goes down. If the count has dropped by 2 or more since the last reading, the daily report's “Google removal” line tells you. A drop of 1 we don't flag, because that's just Google's own churn. The count alone can't tell us exactly which review has gone. You can turn the line on or off on the Report card of the Settings page. The details are in The extra report lines and the monthly summary. If the drop looks suspicious to you, open a case for it on the Disputes page. Disputing reviews with Google shows you how.

s: If your venue's on Tripadvisor, we bring in its reviews from there too, kept apart from the Google numbers.
h: Switching it on What changes then If something goes wrong Switching it off
b: You turn Tripadvisor on one venue at a time, and it's the account owner who can do it. Open the venue's page on Tripadvisor and copy its address from your browser's address bar. It starts like this: “tripadvisor.com/Restaurant_Review-”. In BistroTech, open the Venues page and click the venue's name. On the Tripadvisor card, paste the address into the The venue's Tripadvisor address field. Press the Connect button. The first download takes a few minutes and brings in up to 150 reviews from the last 6 months. The card updates itself in the meantime. After that, we refresh once a day, before the morning report. On the Reviews tab, Tripadvisor reviews have their own mark. Use the All sites picker to show only those, or only the Google ones. In the daily report, new Tripadvisor reviews get their own line. They don't get mixed into the Google numbers. We write replies to these too. We can't post to Tripadvisor, though, so you copy the reply and post it from your Tripadvisor owner account. Posting a reply by hand, without Google access shows you how. Auto-answer never posts a reply to a Tripadvisor review on its own. If the download fails, the card tells you why, and we try again the next morning. If the address isn't a Tripadvisor restaurant page, the card says so and nothing changes. Use the Switch off button on the card. The reviews you already have stay, but no new ones come in.

s: Make a short link and a QR code that guests can use to write you a review on Google.
h: Making a link What the guest sees The rules the link keeps Printing Switching off and deleting
b: You can make a short link with a QR code for any of your venues. Whoever opens it sees the venue's name and a button for writing a review on Google. If you've connected Tripadvisor too, they can write one there as well. The account owner and members can make links. Open the Venues page and click the venue's name. On the Ask for reviews card, type where the link will go, for example “table card”. Only you see this, not the guest. Press the New link button. The Copy link button copies it, and you can send it in a message. The card shows how many times the link was opened in the last 30 days, and next to that, the number of Google reviews over the same period. The two may move together, but that doesn't mean one causes the other. The guest sees a short page that thanks them for coming and asks them to say how it was. It's in their phone's language if that's Hungarian, English, German, French, Italian or Spanish, and in English for anything else. Apart from the language, every guest sees the same thing. We ask everyone the same way. We don't ask first whether they were happy. We don't promise a discount, a gift or anything else in return. Google forbids incentives and may remove reviews because of them. We don't ask the guest to name anyone, and there are no per-waiter codes. The printable card and the QR code download are coming soon. Until then you can try the link and share it, but its address will change later. So for now, don't print the QR code on the screen either. After Switch off, the link only shows a page saying it's no longer active. You can only delete a link once it's switched off, with the Delete button, and that also loses the count of opens.

s: Open a case on suspicious reviews and get a dated document to back up your report to Google.
h: When to open a case Opening a case The document Reporting to Google Afterwards
b: The Disputes page is in the More group of the menu. If the group is closed, open it first. It's the account owner who opens and changes cases. Several one-star reviews came in for a venue in a short time. Guests went back and lowered an earlier rating. Google took reviews off your venue's listing. You want to report a single review. Press the New case button. The last 14 days list shows our alerts and the days your review count fell. If one fits, Use this one fills in the form for you. If you know about something we didn't catch, fill in the Venue, What you are documenting, From this day and To this day fields yourself. Press the Open the case button. In the list of cases, open the case with the Open link. Open the document opens it in a new tab, where you can save it as a PDF using your browser's print option. If you'd rather have a text file, press Download as Markdown. The document has the venue and its Business Profile ID, the period, and the review count day by day. It compares the one-star reviews with the venue's previous 90 days, and quotes every review in the period word for word. At the end come the changed reviews, our alerts and Google's own pages, with the date we read them. The document doesn't claim the reviews are fake. Whether a review comes down is entirely Google's call. You need to send the report yourself. You can report reviews from your Business Profile or from Google's Reviews Management Tool, and you'll have to say which policy they break. If Google turns it down, you can appeal once, with up to 10 reviews in one appeal. Warning: If someone asks for money to take the reviews down, don't pay and don't reply. Google has a separate form for reporting this. In the case's What Google said part, fill in the Status, Google case reference and Notes fields, then press Save. When you set it to filed, we note today's date. Your notes show on the document too. Google doesn't give a deadline for taking a review down.

s: How to look over the finished replies and approve them.
h: Step by step When the card says this
b: We write a reply to every new review with text, and to every review rated 1 to 3 stars, whether or not it has text. Reviews of 4 or 5 stars with no text don't get one. You can narrow this down in Settings, for example to 1 to 3 stars only. By default, no reply goes out without your approval. If you turn on auto-answer (a separate add-on), replies to the reviews you've chosen can go out without it, and by default that's positive reviews only. Open the Replies tab. Next to the tab you can see how many replies are waiting. The worst review comes first. Read it, and you'll find the reply underneath. If the review's in another language, there's a translation under it, and one under the reply too. Edit it if you need to. On a phone, open the Rewrite part first. The Rewrite buttons can make it shorter, warmer or firmer, or switch it to formal or informal address. You can always go back to the original. Press Approve. You can undo it for the next 8 seconds. On a phone the button sits under the reply, and once you've scrolled down to it, it stays handy at the bottom of the screen. If you have added us as a manager on Google and we've accepted the invitation, we'll post the reply within 15 minutes. If not, copy it with the Copy and open Google button and paste it in on Google. Tip: Faster with a keyboard. A approves, S closes without a reply, J and K move, E edits, O opens Google, U undoes. It works on a computer. Press No reply and we'll close the review without a reply. You can still find it later under Reviews. In English and The reply in English (or your account's language): translated just for you. The guest gets the original. If it's folded away, tap its line. Answered on Google: someone replied to this review on Google in the meantime, so this reply isn't needed. Close it with No reply. No longer on Google: the guest or Google took the review down, so you can't reply to it. Close this one with No reply too. We'll also close those last two ourselves as soon as we notice.

s: How to make the replies sound like you, with the rewrite buttons, the voice notes, the rules and the sign-off.
h: The rewrite buttons The voice The rules What we always keep to
b: We write the replies to your settings, always in the guest's language, or in the account's language if the guest only left stars. 4- and 5-star reviews with no text don't get a reply. On the Replies tab, you'll find 5 buttons under the reply: Shorter, Warmer, Firmer, Formal and Informal. On a phone, open the Rewrite part first. Each press is one rewrite, and the new text replaces the old one. The Back to the previous text link brings back the text from before the rewrite. The Restore original link brings back the first version we wrote. A rewritten reply still only goes out when you approve it. If you ask for lots of rewrites within an hour, rewriting pauses for a while. You can still edit the text yourself in the meantime. Open the Settings page and find the Reply voice card. In the Voice field, write how the replies should sound, for example how to address the guest, what to avoid and how to sign off. Press the Save button under the Set-up guide card. You can give a single venue its own notes too. On the Venues page, press the Settings button on the venue's card, and write them in the Voice notes part. On the Reply rules card of the Settings page, you set a few firm rules. This card has its own Save button. Form of address: As the guest wrote (polite when unclear), Always formal or Always informal. Sign-off at the end of a reply: if you leave it empty, the reply ends with the venue's name. You can override it for each venue on the Venues page, in the Sign-off at the end of replies field of the venue's Settings panel. Never write: words, separated by commas. We catch other forms of the words too. If a reply would still contain one of them, that reply isn't made. At most this many words: by default 70 words for a positive review, 120 for a negative one. The rules apply from the next review on, and we don't rewrite replies that are already written. The account owner sets the voice and the rules. We never promise a refund, a discount, free food or any other compensation. We never put a phone number, an email address or a link in a reply. On a negative review we apologise once. We don't argue, and we don't blame the guest.

s: Switch it on, and good reviews get a reply on their own, without anyone reading it first.
h: Turning it on What it means If you extend it to lower reviews Turning it off In the subscription
b: By default, a reply only goes out once you've approved it. Automatic answering takes that over from you, from a star rating you choose upwards. It starts switched off, and only the account owner can turn it on. Open the Settings page and find the Automatic answering card. Turn on the Automatic answering on switch. Choose the threshold. By default the field says Answer automatically from 4 stars up. Press the Save button under the Set-up guide card. Replies to reviews at or above the stars you set don't wait for approval. We post them to Google within a quarter of an hour, and nobody reads them first. 4- and 5-star reviews with no text don't get a reply, so nothing goes out to them automatically either. Replies to lower reviews still wait for you on the Replies tab. Replies posted this way are marked “automatic” in the list and in the history. It only covers Google reviews. Replies to Tripadvisor reviews always wait for your approval. It only works if the Reply writing on switch on the Replies card is on as well. We can only post the reply where you've added us as a manager on your Google Business Profile and we've accepted the invitation. Anywhere else the reply's still written, but you'll need to paste it in yourself (see Adding us as a manager on Google). Warning: If you set the threshold to 3 stars or lower, lower reviews get a reply on their own too, and nobody reads it first. It appears on your own Google Business Profile, where your guests see it. The Settings page warns you about this on the card too, when you pick a threshold like that. A bad reply to a negative review is public. It's worth seeing how your replies sound first, by approving them yourself. Rewriting and the reply rules can help with that. Turn off the Automatic answering on switch and press the Save button. Replies that have already gone out stay on Google, but every new reply waits for your approval again. The Activity page records it whenever it's turned on or off. On the Subscription page, you'll find it among the add-ons as Auto-answer. Its price hasn't been announced yet.

t: Posting a reply by hand, without Google access
s: If you haven't added us as a manager, you copy the finished reply with one button and paste it in on Google yourself.
h: Step by step If you have no time now For a Tripadvisor review Worth knowing
b: Without manager access to a venue's Google Business Profile, we can't post the reply for you. We still write it, and you still approve it. The only difference is that you paste it in. On the Replies tab, approve the reply with the Approve button. The reply is ready panel appears. Press the Copy and open Google button. The reply is copied to your clipboard, and the review opens on Google in a new tab. On Google, paste the text in as your reply and send it. If we don't have a link to the review, the panel shows the Copy reply button instead. You'll then need to find the review in your Google Business Profile yourself. Press the Later button. The reply waits for you on the Replies tab, in the Approved, not yet posted list, marked “post it by hand”. Pick it up from there whenever you like, with the Copy reply button and the Open on Google link. We can't post to Tripadvisor. You'll see the Copy and open Tripadvisor button there, and you post the reply from your Tripadvisor owner account. We can't see that you've posted the reply by hand. So it stays on the approved list, and on our side the review still looks unanswered. If you'd rather not post replies by hand, add us as a manager. Here's how: Adding us as a manager on Google.

s: The Analysis tab shows what keeps coming up in what guests write, and how your venues compare side by side.
h: The main numbers The two charts Themes Staff mentions Venue comparison
b: The Analysis tab shows the numbers for a period, venue by venue. Pick the period at the top: 7 days, 30 days or 90 days. New reviews and Average of new reviews: the reviews that came in during the period. 1-star or 2-star share: the percentage of new reviews rated 1 or 2 stars. Unanswered negatives: reviews of 3 stars or fewer with no owner reply. Reviews analysed: what percentage of the new reviews we've analysed so far. Google rating over time: for each venue, from the daily check. Click a venue's name to hide its line or bring it back. New reviews per day: all venues together. Under each one, the Show as table link gives you the same thing in numbers. We read the reviews with text to see what they're about, like the service, the wait or the prices. Under Themes you'll find two lists, What guests praise and What guests complain about. Each shows the 10 most common themes. A review counts towards a theme only once. A theme counts as a complaint when it comes up in a review with a negative tone, or in one rated 3 stars or fewer. It counts as praise when it comes up in a review with a positive tone, or in one rated 4 stars or more. For each theme, you can see at which venues it came up most. Each theme gets one consistent name, so you can compare themes across venues and languages. This table lists the staff that guests named, spelled the way the guests wrote them. A mention counts as positive in a 4-star or 5-star review, and negative in a review of 3 stars or fewer. You'll find the details on the Recognition page, as Recognition and staff mentions explains. The last table puts your venues side by side. Its columns are new reviews, average, one-star and two-star reviews, unanswered negatives, the Google rating now, change, and total reviews. The change is the difference between the first and last daily check of the period.

t: What guests write about each dish
s: The Dishes page shows which dishes guests mention at each venue, and in what kind of review.
h: The table Sorting As the guest wrote it If the table is empty
b: The Dishes page is in the More group of the menu. If the group is closed, open it. It shows, venue by venue, what guests mention by name from your menu. Choose the period at the top: 30 days or 90 days. Each row is one dish at one venue. The Mentions column shows how many reviews named the dish. The Positive and Negative columns show how many reviews spoke well of it, and how many badly. The Average is the star average of the reviews that named the dish. Click a heading to sort the table. Sort by dish to bring each dish's venue rows together, so you can compare where it turns out better. If the same dish does very differently at 2 venues, it's worth a look in the kitchen. Dishes show up the way guests wrote them, in their own language. We don't translate them or match them to your menu, so “gulyás”, “goulash” and “gulasch” are 3 separate rows. We collect dishes from analysed reviews shortly after a review reaches us. We don't analyse older reviews, so a new account won't have many dishes on the list in its first few days.

s: Who guests mention by name, and how to fold different spellings of one person's name together.
h: The table Name spellings Download Where else you see the names
b: The Recognition page is in the More group of the menu. If the group is closed, open it first. It lists the names guests wrote in their reviews, with a separate row for each venue. Choose the period at the top: 7 days, 30 days or 90 days. Mentions shows how many reviews named the person. The Positive and Negative columns show the mood of the whole review the name came up in, not of the sentence about the person. The Other column holds neutral reviews and ones we haven't analysed yet. The What guests wrote button lets you read the mentions themselves. Use this list to thank people for praise, not to appraise your staff. By default it's sorted by the number of mentions. The negative column is shown too, and you can click any column's header to sort by it. Guests spell the same person's name in different ways. On the Name spellings card, you tell us which spelling means whom. Type the name in the The name to show in the list field, for example “Roland”. Type the spelling in the How guests write it field, for example “Roli”. Press the Add button. From then on, the list shows them as one row. The account owner manages the name spellings. The Download as a spreadsheet button saves the list to a file, filtered and sorted just as you see it on screen. The daily report's analysis lists the staff who were mentioned, by name, and the weekly summary has the names mentioned most. A card on the Today tab can also let you know when someone's been praised several times this week.

t: Your rank on Google Maps and your competitors
s: See where you come in the Maps results for a search, and how the restaurants nearby are doing.
h: The search phrase and the starting point Adding a phrase The table of positions Competitors The weekly rank summary
b: The Rank page is in the More group of the menu, so open the group first if it's closed. The account owner adds search phrases and competitors. The search phrase is what a guest would type into Google Maps, for example “goulash budapest”. The starting point is the spot on the map we measure the search from. We need it because Google puts places near the person searching first. If you have no phrase yet, press the Add the first phrase button. After that you work on the New search phrase card. In the Search phrase field, type what a guest would search for. In the Name of the starting point field, give the point a name, for example “Deák tér”. Open Maps with the Open Google Maps to find coordinates link. Right-click the point a guest would search from (on a phone, press and hold it), and copy the two numbers. Paste them into the Latitude (lat) and Longitude (lng) fields. You can also paste both at once into the first field. Press the Add phrase button. We measure once every morning, so you'll see a new phrase's result after the next morning run. You can have up to 30 active phrases at a time. For each phrase you see the position, how it's changed over 7 days, and the day it was measured. If the venue isn't in the top 20, we tell you. The History button shows the earlier measurements. Switch off leaves the phrase out of the morning run, and its earlier data stays. The Competitors board is at the bottom of the Rank page. It puts your venue next to up to 5 places nearby, so you can see their rating, how many reviews they have, how many they've gained, and their positions in your search results. Press the Add a competitor button. The list shows the places that came up for your phrases in the last 30 days. Press the Add button next to the one you want to watch. Switch on Daily competitor watch. While the watch is off, we don't look anything up, and the board shows the earlier measurements. Once it's on, we check the rating and review count of the places you added every morning. The Remove button takes a place off the board, but its earlier measurements stay. On Mondays there's also a summary of your positions. It goes to the Marketing destination on Telegram, if you've connected it. There's more on this in The weekly summary.

s: Ask about your own reviews and numbers, and the assistant shows you what it based the answer on.
h: Asking What it can do for you
b: The Assistant page is in the More group of the menu (open the group if it's closed). It answers from your own account's data: the reviews, the daily numbers, the replies written, the themes and the positions. If there's no data for something, it'll tell you. Press the New question button, or pick one of the suggested questions, for example “What happened this week?” Type the question and press the Send button. Enter sends it too, and Shift with Enter starts a new line. Above the answer you'll see the rows it worked from (reviews, daily numbers, names, themes), so you know where every number came from. You get a set number of questions a day, and the page shows how many you've used today. Conversations are kept, so you can pick up any of them again from the Conversations list. The assistant can approve or skip a reply, and post one you've already approved to Google. It only does that when you've asked it to in your own message. It uses your login, so it can't do anything you aren't allowed to do. It won't rewrite a reply's text. If you want to change it, do that on the Replies tab. It can write a suggestion for your listing, but it doesn't change anything on Google by itself. The suggestion waits for you on the Listing page, and you decide there. Tip: If guests or colleagues call one of your venues something else, add its old name or nickname on the Settings page, in the What the assistant should know about your venues field. Then it'll still understand the question.

s: The Listing page shows what your Google Business Profile says about you, what's gone stale on it, and what we suggest.
h: What you see for each venue The suggestions Writing to Google
b: You'll find the Listing page in the More group of the menu. If the group is closed, open it first. It only works for restaurants where you've added us as a manager on your Google Business Profile. Adding us as a manager on Google shows you how. Last read: when we last read the listing. Description: how many characters it has. Opening hours: whether they're published. Special hours in 30 days, Photos and Open suggestions. Reviews mentioning hours: how many reviews brought up your opening hours in the past 30 days. We don't read the listing on our own. The account owner starts it with the Read the listing button, and the suggestions update after that. Suggestions come from the numbers we already hold. You'll get one when guests found the door locked while the listing said the venue was open. You'll also get one when a public holiday is coming up with no special hours set, when the description is short or old, or when there aren't many photos. And from the week's good reviews, we'll suggest a weekly post. The weekly post is the only one we write text for. For the rest, you see what the listing says now and what made us flag it. We won't guess your opening hours. The account owner decides with Approve or Drop it. Writing to Google isn't switched on yet. An approved suggestion stays put, and the card tells you it hasn't gone out. Nothing goes from this page to Google today.

s: Bring colleagues into your account with an invite link or by email, and choose their role and which venues they see as you go.
h: Invite link Another link, or a replacement Inviting by email address Pending invitations If they are already in the account Inviting a viewer
b: The account owner invites colleagues from the Team page. You'll find it in the Account group of the menu. On the Create an invite link card, use the Role field to choose whether they'll be a Member, an Owner or a Viewer. Under Venues, decide what they'll see. All of them gives them every venue, including ones you add later. To give them just a few, untick All of them and tick the venues you want. Press the Create link button. Copy the link with the Copy link button. Do it now, because we can't show it to you again later. Send it to your colleague in a message. The link works for 7 days and can be used to join once. You'll only see the Venues part once the account has a venue. An owner always sees every venue, so there's nothing to choose for one. When your colleague opens the link, they'll see the account's name, their role and their venues. If they don't have a login yet, they sign up with the Sign up button and land straight in the account. If they already have one, they use I have an account, sign in, and they're in just as quickly. And if they open the link while already signed in, the Join account button is all it takes. Above the finished link, the card shows which role and venues it gives. Another link makes one more link with the same access, and the earlier one keeps working. That way you can invite several colleagues, each with their own link. Replace link stops the earlier link straight away and gives you a new one in its place. Use it if you sent the link to the wrong person. If you change the Role or the Venues after making the link, it disappears from the card but keeps working. You'll find it under Pending invitations, where you can revoke it. If your colleague already has a BistroTech login, you can invite them by email address too. On the Invite someone card, type their address in the Email address field and choose their role. For a member or a viewer, pick their venues under Venues, just as you would for a link. Press the Invite button. Tell them to sign in. Next time they do, they'll be in the account, with the venues you chose. For anyone who doesn't have a login yet, send the invite link instead. Invitations nobody has used yet are in the Pending invitations list, with the role, the venues and the expiry date. You can cancel any of them with the Revoke button. If you've deleted every venue an invitation names, the list shows “No venue left” next to it. Nobody can join with it any more, so revoke it and make a new one. If the person you're inviting is already on the account, the invitation won't change anything. Their role and venues stay as they are. You can change those on the Team page, as Roles and access per venue explains. A viewer can look but can't change anything. They see every venue, or only the ones you tick on the invitation. You can invite one by link or by email address. Just choose Viewer in the Role field. There's more about roles in Roles and access per venue.

s: Who can see and do what in the account, and how to give a colleague access to just a few venues.
h: The three roles Changing a role Access per venue Removing and leaving Activity
b: Everyone on the account has a role. You manage roles and access on the Team page, in the Account group of the menu. Owner: sees and can do everything. Owners invite and remove people, add and switch off venues, change the settings, and pick the package. Member: sees every page and can work on replies, so they can approve, skip and rewrite them. They can't change the account settings. Viewer: sees everything, but can't change anything. The owner changes someone's role on the Team page, in the Role column of that colleague's row. The last owner can't be removed, and their role can't be changed. If that's what you're after, make someone else an owner first. On the Team page, in the colleague's row, press the Edit link in the Venue column. Untick All of them, and tick the venues they're allowed to see. Press the Save button. Someone who doesn't see every venue only sees the reviews and replies for their own venues. They won't see the account's totals, the team or the activity log. The owner always sees every venue. You can also pick the venues on the invitation itself, so the colleague joins with just those from the start. See Inviting colleagues. The owner takes a colleague off the account with the Remove button in their row. From then on, that colleague can't get to the reviews. To leave the account, use the Leave this account link. An owner can invite you back later. The Activity page shows who did what in the account. You'll see replies, changes to the team and the venues, settings and invitations. Use the buttons at the top to filter, for example to the Replies or Team area.

s: If you run several accounts, the Group page puts their numbers in one table and writes a weekly summary about them.
h: A new account Creating a group The account's consent What the group sees Weekly summary about the group Deleting a group
b: One account can hold several venues, and you don't need a group for that. A group is for when you've got several separate accounts, say one per company, and want to see them together. If you own an account, you can create another one from the account part of the menu. That way one login runs several accounts. Click the New account link. On a computer it's under the account's name, on a phone behind the Menu button. Fill in the Account name field, and check the Time zone and Language fields. Press the Create account button. The new account opens straight away, and it starts with a 14-day trial too. The First steps guide walks you through adding a venue. You switch between your accounts in the Account field, which appears once you've got 2 accounts. One email address can own up to 3 accounts. Open the Group page in the Account group of the menu. On the New group card, fill in The group name field and press the Create the group button. In the Accounts part, choose the account from the Account to add list, and press the Add an account button. You can only add accounts you own. Each account decides for itself whether to share its summary, on the Group sharing card of its own Settings page. The account owner picks Share it or Do not share. If an account doesn't share, the group sees nothing of it. In the Per account table, each account gets one row. It shows the new reviews, the average, the negative reviews waiting for a reply, the changed reviews and changes in rank. You choose the period with the 7 days and 30 days buttons. The group only sees counts and averages. No reviews, no guest names and no replies. Every Monday morning there's a summary about the group too, with the most important things to do. If you fill in the Telegram chat id field on the Group settings card, we'll send it there. If you leave it empty, you can read it under Latest weekly summary. To find the chat's id, connect the same chat to one of the accounts, then look on that account's Settings page. First take the accounts out of the group with the Remove it button. Then, on the Group settings card, press Delete the group, and then Delete it. Your accounts, venues and reviews aren't touched.

s: On the My login page you change your password and turn on two-step sign-in. You can sign out of your other devices there too.
h: Two-step sign-in Changing your password Signing out of other devices
b: The My login page is about your own login, not the venues' account. To open it, click your own email address in the menu. With this on, you'll need a 6-digit code as well as your password. The code comes from an authenticator app on your phone, such as Google Authenticator. So even if your password leaks, nobody can sign in to your account with it. On the Two-step sign-in card, press the Turn on button. Scan the code that appears with the authenticator app, or type the key in by hand. Type the app's 6-digit code and press the Check and turn on button. From then on, we'll ask for the code after your password when you sign in. If the code isn't accepted, check that your phone's clock is right. You turn it off with the Turn off button, which needs a fresh code too. Warning: If you lose the phone with the authenticator app on it, you can't sign in by yourself, and only we can turn off two-step sign-in. So save the key somewhere else as well, for example in a password manager. On the Password card, type your current password in the Current password field. Type the new one in the New password and New password again fields. It must be at least 8 characters. If you want to sign out of your other devices too, tick the Also sign me out on other devices box. Press the Change password button. Lost your phone, or left BistroTech open on a shared computer? Press the Sign out on all other devices button on the Other devices card. You'll stay signed in on the device you're using now.

t: Downloading your data and deleting the account
s: How to download the account's data or your own, and how to delete a venue, the account or your login if you need to.
h: The account's data Your own data Deleting a venue Deleting the account Deleting your login
b: You can download the account's data and your own login data whenever you like. There are three things you can delete: a venue, the account, or your own login. The account owner downloads it from the Download the account's data card at the bottom of the Settings page. All data (JSON): the venues, the reviews with their analysis, the replies and the settings, all in one file. Reviews as a spreadsheet (CSV): just the reviews, as a table. An account set to English separates the columns with commas, one set to Hungarian with semicolons, so Excel in the same language opens it straight away. On the My login page, the Download my data button gets you your login's data. That's your email address, the day you signed up, your accounts and the date you accepted the terms. On the Venues page, press the Settings button on the venue's card. Open the Delete the venue part, and type the venue's name. Press the Delete for good button, and confirm. That deletes every review, reply and statistic of the venue for good. If you only want a break, switch it off with the Active box instead, and nothing's lost. At the bottom of the Settings page, on the Delete the account card, type your password and the account's name. Press the Delete the account button, and confirm. We then mark the account for deletion. The daily report stops straight away, and the account disappears for everyone on the team. You've got 30 days to bring it back, from the Accounts awaiting deletion card on the My login page, with the Restore button. After that it's deleted for good. Warning: If you want to keep the account's data, download it first. Once it's deleted for good, we can't give it back. The Delete my login card on the My login page deletes only your own login, not the venues' account. If you're the only owner of an account, make someone else an owner first, or delete that account. Type your password, and type “DELETE” in the field. Press the Delete my login button, and confirm. Your login is deleted straight away and for good. Your name and email address do stay next to the Internal notes you wrote on reviews, and on the accounts' Activity page for 180 days. If you'd like those deleted too, call us or write to our registered address (it's at the bottom of the page).

s: Choose how BistroTech looks for you, and which language you see it in.
h: Where you set it Three steps, in order Light or dark In the Glass style only Motion and sounds The language
b: Everyone sets their own appearance, so your colleagues see theirs, not yours. Your choice is saved with your login, so it looks the same on your other devices. On the Appearance card of the Settings page. Changes show up straight away, and there's nothing to save. Style, meaning the shapes. Pop has thick outlines, hard shadows and blocks of colour. Glass puts frosted panels over a soft glow of colour. Classic is restrained, with fine lines on a paper-white background. Colours. You'll only see the colours of the style you picked. Pop has Lemon, Aperol, Matcha, Gelato, Balaton and the dark Midnight. Glass has Market, Aperol, Gelato, Balaton, Matcha, and the dark Neon and Paprika. Classic has Classic and Classic night. Font. Pick the typeface for headings and numbers from the style's own set. Body text uses the same face in every style. By default, you'll see Pop with automatic colours and Space Grotesk. Pick Light, Dark or Automatic. Automatic follows your device's setting, so in Pop you'll see Lemon by day and Midnight at night. The Glass switch sets where the glass effect goes: Off, On the menu or On the cards too. Next to it are the Blur and Opacity sliders. Back to the default puts you back on Pop, automatic colours and Space Grotesk. The Motion row sets how much moves on screen: Calm: only what you start moves. Lively: new things and feedback move once. Nothing repeats. Playful: there's slow movement in the background too, like the band of yesterday's reviews on Today. You can pause it anytime. Automatic: Playful, unless your device asks for less motion. Playful is only in the Pop style. Glass and Classic go up to Lively. If your device asks for less motion, nothing moves on its own, whatever you choose. At the Playful level, Pause motion stops all automatic movement at once. It's at the bottom of the left sidebar, or under Menu on a phone. The band of yesterday's reviews has its own Pause button too. Sounds is Off by default. Set it to On and you'll hear a short sound when you approve, skip, undo or switch something. It won't play on its own, and it won't tell you anything the screen doesn't. You set the language of the pages with the Language menu, to Magyar or English. That's your own setting too. The daily report's language is separate. It comes from the Language field on the Account card of the Settings page, and it applies to everyone in the account.

s: The Subscription page shows 3 packages. What goes in each, and what they'll cost, isn't final yet.
h: The three packages The band Add-ons Asking for a quote Billing details and invoices Usage
b: The packages are on the Subscription page, in the Account group of the menu. You can also get there from the Plan card on the Settings page. Only the account owner can choose a package. The Starter, Analyst and Full cards show what's in each one. Monitoring, the daily report and the written replies come with all three. What goes in each package, and the price, aren't final yet. That's why every package says “Price soon”. During the trial, everything works whichever package you're on. The page also shows how many active venues the account has, and which band that puts it in (1 venue, 2 to 9, or 10 or more). How the band affects the price isn't final yet. You can add Auto-answer to any package. Listing care and Competitor benchmark don't have a price yet, so they say “Coming”. Pick the package with the Choose this button, and tick the add-ons. Press the Request a quote button. We'll note what you picked. You won't pay anything here for now. If it's urgent, write to us with the Feedback button. On the Billing details card you tell us who to invoice: the company name, tax number, address, and the email address for invoices. The Invoices list is at the bottom of the page. We don't invoice during the trial. At the bottom of the Settings page, the Usage card shows how many reviews we fetched, and how many count checks, analysis runs and sent messages there were this month, last month and over the last 6 months. It shows counts only, with no price or cost.

s: Use a new account free for 14 days, with no bank card, on your own venues' real reviews.
h: What you get Where you see how far you are After the trial
b: The 14 days start from when you create the account. You don't need a bank card, and there's no minimum term. You get the full base package, working on your own venues' real reviews. We gather the reviews, write the replies, and prepare a daily report every day. We don't invoice you during the trial. You can add up to 5 venues during the trial, counting any you've switched off. If you hit the limit, the page tells you. If you need more, ask for a demo on the website, or write to us with the Feedback button in the menu. On the Settings page, below the Save button, the Plan card shows your plan and how many days you have left. It shows when the trial ends in your own time zone. In the last few days, a marker also shows up in the menu and takes you to the Settings page. Right now nothing stops when the trial ends. The daily report and everything else keep running. We haven't decided yet what the rule will be later. When we do, you'll read it here. For the packages, see Packages and billing.
